extracted.intended_audience: general readers interested in comedy, celebrity news, and #MeToo issues
extracted.subtask_description: A short news feature reporting on protests and controversy surrounding a comedian's public return after sexual-misconduct allegations, including voices of protestors, peers, and venue responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support signals prioritizing laughter over victims
rubrics_metrics.description: When you support Louis CK, you tell women your laughter is more important than their sexual assaults and loss of their careers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This wording (from a protestor's sign) is presented as an evaluative claim: choosing to attend or promote a comedian accused of sexual misconduct sends a message about whose wellbeing is being prioritized. Use this as a moral/evaluative yardstick when deciding whether to endorse or attend a performer's comeback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize harmed comedians before allowing offender back on stage
rubrics_metrics.description: "Every female comedian he has harmed deserves a place on the Comedy Cellar stage one hundred times before he should be allowed back on the stage."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted from protestor Jennifer Boudinot, this sets a concrete standard for venue programming: restore opportunities to those harmed by the offender multiple times before reinstating that offender. It functions as a suggested sequencing/prioritization policy for venues and promoters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Care with self-referential jokes about misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: CK made light references to his behaviour; he opened by asking about people's year and then repeated jokes referencing his financial loss and trouble since the allegations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article highlights that the comedian reused and downplayed his misconduct in jokes. This implies a criterion for comedic content: whether a performer addresses allegations in a way that trivializes harm or centers their own loss (which may affect public reception). Consider whether such jokes are reparative, self-aware, or dismissive when evaluating a comeback set.

rubrics_metrics.name: Venue transparency about booking controversial performers
rubrics_metrics.description: We’ve taken a lot of criticism for surprising people with his unannounced performances. I’m afraid now we will be criticised for the opposite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement from Comedy Cellar owner Noam Dworman frames a programming tradeoff: surprise bookings can draw criticism for hiding controversial appearances; announced bookings invite protest but allow public debate. Use transparency about billing as an operational criterion when evaluating venue decisions around contentious acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peers' public response as a legitimacy signal
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple female comedians – including Aisling Bea, Mae Martin, Aparna Nancherla and Siobhan Thompson – have all spoken out against CK’s return.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article presents fellow comedians' objections as relevant context. The collective stance of peers functions as an evaluative factor for whether a comeback is socially acceptable; widespread professional dissent can be treated as a negative indicator when assessing a performer's return.
